VS128.desc: Same field as VD128, read as a source (3rd source of vmaddfp128/vnmsubfp128/vmaddcfp128/vsel128)

VD3D0.desc: vpkd3d128 D3D data type: 0 D3DCOLOR, 1 NORMSHORT2, 2 NORMPACKED32 (2_10_10_10), 3 FLOAT16_2, 4 NORMSHORT4, 5 FLOAT16_4, 6 NORMPACKED64 (4_20_20_20). Meaning from xenia's emitter; every value seen in real code is in 0-5

VD3D1.desc: vpkd3d128 pack size: 1 = 32-bit result, 2/3 = 64-bit result (xenia). With VD3D0 it forms the 5-bit immediate (VD3D0<<2 | VD3D1)

VD3D2.desc: vpkd3d128: which word slot of VD receives the packed result (xenia: "shift"); vrlimi128: rotate-left amount in words, 0-3

legacy_vmx_not_implemented.note: IBM: VMX128 is binary-compatible with a subset of VMX; the rest raise the illegal-instruction handler. IBM does not list them; "unsupported" = named by the 2007 GCC list; "unconfirmed" = xenia only. See the top-level "hardware" block for what a real console did with both lists.

illegal_but_not_dropped.dcba: optional in the table (arch-opt); not implemented on the console
illegal_but_not_dropped.fre: optional in the table (arch-opt); not implemented on the console
illegal_but_not_dropped.frsqrtes: optional in the table (arch-opt); not implemented on the console
illegal_but_not_dropped.lvsl128: listed by xenia, the binutils patch and the Ghidra fork, never seen in real code; the console raises an illegal-instruction interrupt on every case
illegal_but_not_dropped.lvsr128: listed by xenia, the binutils patch and the Ghidra fork, never seen in real code; the console raises an illegal-instruction interrupt on every case
illegal_but_not_dropped.mcrxr: implemented by the Xenon LLE; the console raises an illegal-instruction interrupt on every case
illegal_but_not_dropped.popcntb: optional in the table (arch-opt); not implemented on the console

timing.method: Cycles per instruction from the slope between two unroll depths of a 20,000-iteration loop, converted from the timebase at 64 core cycles per tick (full speed). latency: one dependent chain, all values 1. issue: 16 overlapped chains. fixed_operands: 8 independent instructions reading two fixed source registers, with the named data set. Measured with the other hardware thread of the core running libxenon's idle loop, with MSR[SF]=1, interrupts off.
caveats: tied-accumulator ops (vmaddfp128, vnmsubfp128, vmaddcfp128, vmaddfp, ...) feed themselves in the fixed-operand runs, so their fixed figures are bounded by latency/8 chains; use `issue`
divide and multiply were only tried with the `normal` and `wide` GPR data sets; divw/divwu operate on the low 32 bits, which the wide set does not exercise

opcode_sweep.note: Words are primary | register-field pattern | every value of the low `bits` bits; register fields are not enumerated.

hardware.not_tested: branches, sc, privileged instructions, SPR access, lmw/stmw, string ops, eciwx/ecowx (see hwtest/README.md)

microarchitecture.note: From the hwtest timing plans (hwtest/findings/<plan>.json, made by hwtest/host/findings.py from a console run; decision rules in hwtest/host/analysis_timing.py). Parts whose plan has not run are absent.

classes.br_t: bc 12,2,.+4 taken to the next word
classes.ld: ld from an L1 line (chain: pointer chase ld r,0(r))
classes.lwz: lwz from an L1 line (chain: pointer chase lwz r,0(r))

dual_issue.rule: Analyser: host/analysis_timing.py. Each of 22 instruction classes alone and every unordered pair interleaved (A0 B0 A1 B1 ...), variants tput (K rotating registers per class) and chain (one register). overlap = (A(a)+A(b)-P)/min(A(a),A(b)): >= 0.8 together, <= 0.2 serial; confident when the class does not change within the noise (3% / 0.05 cycles per value).

cited: [FPF] L1 D 32 KB 4-way, L2 1 MB 8-way shared
[AB06] 128-byte lines in all L1 and L2

store_behaviour.caveat: write-allocate WITHOUT store-to-load forwarding from a pending miss would look the same; write-through itself is not visible in these timings
store_behaviour.cited: [FPF] L1 D-cache 32 KB, 4-way, 128-byte lines, write-through, no allocate on a store miss
store_behaviour.why: a load after a store miss pays 73.8 cycles extra (~ one L2 access, L2-L1 = 40.2): the missed store did not leave its line in L1 and was not forwarded from a store buffer

xdcbt.cited: [FPF], [AB06] xdcbt prefetches into the L1 D-cache and never puts the line in L2
xdcbt.why: dcbt reference reloads from L2 (expected L2): the 6 loads did not evict the line from L1 as assumed

evidence: [AB06] 128-byte lines in all CPU L1 and L2 caches
hardware (memlat): conflict strides consistent with 4-way, set stride 8K (=> 32K) for L1

mispredict.assumption: 50% mispredicts (the predictor cannot learn xorshift64's sign bit); addi cost = latency.json addi issue

branch_history.interpretation: [FPF] branch history table 4 KB, 2-way set-associative, per thread. Its capacity in branches depends on the entry format, which no held source gives (e.g. 16K 2-bit counters or 32K 1-bit); the knee is reported in branches, not converted.
